title: Charge and current
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:36Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: None of the bank points defines current as the rate of flow of charge (I = q/t); they cover electric fields, magnetic forces, wire forces and Millikan's oil drop, which only use charge and current in passing.

draft.title: Charge and current
card: Electric charge is measured in coulombs (C). In a metal wire, the moving charges are electrons.
Current is the rate at which charge flows past a point. I = q/t, where q is charge in coulombs and t is time in seconds.
Current is measured in amperes (A). One ampere is one coulomb passing a point each second.
A larger current means more charge passes each second. The same current for a longer time moves more charge in total.
draft.remember: Current is charge per second: I = q/t, and 1 A is 1 C each second.

a.q: A phone charger cable carries a steady 2 A. How much charge passes a point in the cable each second?
a.why: One ampere is one coulomb per second, so 2 A means 2 C passes each second. 0.5 C comes from dividing the wrong way round.
a.clue: Think of an ampere as coulombs each second.

b.q: A torch in Bendigo has a steady current of 0.50 A. How much charge passes through the bulb in 2.0 minutes?
b.why: Time must be in seconds: 2.0 min = 120 s. Then q = It = 0.50 × 120 = 60 C. Using 2.0 for the time gives 1.0 C, which is the tempting mistake.
